title: Spatiotemporal characterization of endothelial cell motility and physical forces during exposure to Borrelia burgdorferi
protocol: Add 9 mL of complete BSK-H medium to a 15 mL falcon tube.
Further add 1.5 mL of frozen Bb stock culture to the tube.
Place the tube at 33°C until the concentration of Bb reaches 2–5 × 10^6 bacteria/mL (mid log phase).
Dilute the Bb solution to 1 × 10^3 bacteria/mL once mid-log phase is reached.
Grow Bb in fresh complete BSK-H at 33°C until reaching a density of approximately 5 × 10^7 Bb/mL.
Incubate the desired amount of bacteria from step 5 at 56°C for 30 minutes to heat-inactivate Bb.
Store heat-inactivated Bb at 4°C.
Activate glass coverslips of 24-well glass bottom plates.
Add 500 μL of 1 M NaOH on glass coverslips and incubate at 21°C–24°C for 30 min.
Rinse the wells once with ultrapure water.
Add 500 μL of 2% (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane in 95% ethanol to each well and incubate at 21°C–24°C for 5 min.
Rinse the wells once with ultrapure water.
Incubate each well with 500 μL of 0.5% glutaraldehyde in water at 21°C–24°C for 30 min to 2 h.
Rinse the wells once with ultrapure water.
Dry the coverslips by placing the multi-well plate on a 60°C warm metal plate with the lid slightly off, or allow to dry at 21°C–24°C until completely dry.

Prepare two aqueous solutions in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes that contain 5% acrylamide and 0.1% bisacrylamide by adding 152.6 μL water, 23.125 μL of 40% acrylamide, and 9.25 μL of 2% bisacrylamide to each tube.
In a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 149.6 μL water, 23.125 μL of 40% acrylamide, 9.25 μL of 2% bisacrylamide, and 3 μL of 0.2 μm tracer fluorescent beads to prepare Solution 2.
Optional: Degas all four solutions using vacuum for 15 min to eliminate oxygen that inhibits polymerization.
Pipette 1.2 μL of 10% APS stock and 0.8 μL of TEMED to Solution 1 to initiate polymerization and mix well by pipetting up and down.
Immediately after, add 3.6 μL of Solution 1 to the center of each glass coverslip in a 24-well dish.
Cover/sandwich the polyacrylamide droplets with a 12 mm untreated circular coverslip using forceps.
Let Solution 1 sit for 20 min or until it fully polymerizes.
Mix 1.2 μL of 10% APS stock with 0.8 μL of TEMED in Solution 2.
Add 2.4 μL of the mixed Solution 2 to the center of each hydrogel in the well of a 24-well dish without touching the gels.
Cover Solution 2 with 12-mm circular glass coverslips.
Gently press downwards using forceps to minimize the thickness of the second layer.
Let Solution 2 polymerize for 20 minutes.
Add 200 μL of water to each well to facilitate removal of the glass coverslips.
Remove the glass coverslips using a hooked syringe needle and forceps.
Add 1 mL of 50 mM HEPES pH 7.5 to each well to keep hydrogels hydrated.
UV-expose the hydrogels for 1 hour in the tissue culture hood, ensuring the lid is inverted.
Store the plate with hydrogels at 4°C indefinitely, wrapped with parafilm to prevent evaporation and dehydration.
Weigh 10 mg of Sulfo-SANPAH and place it in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Add 100 μL DMSO to the Sulfo-SANPAH and mix well until dissolved.
Mix 10 mL of 50 mM HEPES buffer (pH 7.5) with the dissolved Sulfo-SANPAH solution.
Remove HEPES buffer from the hydrogels and add 200 μL of the Sulfo-SANPAH solution to them.
Expose the hydrogels to UV light at 302 nm for 10 minutes.
Wash the hydrogels twice with 1 mL of 50 mM HEPES buffer (pH 7.5).
Prepare a 0.25 mg/mL solution of rat tail collagen I in 50 mM HEPES buffer (pH 7.5).
Add 200 μL of the collagen I solution to each hydrogel.
Wash any excess crosslinker from the hydrogels as needed.
Incubate the hydrogels, with the collagen solution on top, for 16–18 hours at 21°C–24°C.
Place multi-well plates in secondary containment to prevent dehydration/evaporation.
Add laboratory cleaning tissues soaked in water around the inner periphery of the containment.
Wash the hydrogels once with PBS buffer to remove excess collagen.
Equilibrate hydrogels with cell culture media at 37°C for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Seed ECs on equilibrated hydrogels.
Incubate seeded ECs for 24 hours to form a confluent cell monolayer.
Transfer the multi-well plate into the insert stage of an epifluorescence microscope.
Conduct time-lapse imaging recordings for 24 hours post-exposure.
Add live or heat-inactivated Bb spirochetes around 5 hours after initiating recordings.
If TFM is performed, add sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) at the end of the recording to acquire a reference image of tracer beads in undeformed hydrogels where cells have been removed.
Stain EC nuclei with Hoechst to characterize cell kinematics.
First wash the cells and their culture flask once with sterile PBS.
Add 2 mL of 0.05% trypsin/EDTA on a 75-cm flask.
Incubate the flask at 37°C for 5–10 min to allow cell detachment from the substrate.
Neutralize the trypsin by adding 10 mL of cell culture medium containing FBS.
Pipette gently to break up clumps of cells, and then place the solution into a conical centrifuge tube.
Take out 10 μL of the solution and very gently fill out the chamber underneath the coverslip of a glass hemocytometer to count cells.
Pellet down the solution of cells contained in the conical centrifuge tube using centrifugation for 5 min at 200 × g.
During the 5 min waiting period, count the cells using the hemocytometer.
Resuspend the cells in MCDB-131 full medium at a concentration of 4 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Seed the cells in suspension on the hydrogels by removing the medium from the hydrogels.
Add 1 mL of cell suspension to each hydrogel.
Mix 1:100 collagen I solution (stock concentration is 3.1 mg/mL) in PBS and add 500 μL to each well if not using TFM.
Incubate the multi-well plate with collagen for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Wash the coated wells once with PBS if using glass coverslips coated with collagen I.
Seed ECs on glass coverslips as you would on hydrogels.
Let cells reside on the hydrogels or glass coverslips for 24 hours to form a confluent monolayer.
Prepare a solution of 1 μg/mL Hoechst in cell culture media.
Remove the medium from the cells after 24 hours.
Add 1 mL of Hoechst containing medium to the cells.
Place the multi-well plate in the incubator for 10 minutes.
Aspirate out the Hoechst containing medium after staining.
Wash the cells once with PBS.
Mix 1 mL of warm live-microscopy medium by supplementing Leibovitz’s L-15 with 10% fetal bovine serum, 10 ng/mL of EGF, and 1 μg/mL hydrocortisone.
Turn on the epifluorescence (or confocal microscope).
Set the microscope incubator's temperature to 37°C for at least 30 min before starting microscopy recording.
Place the multi-well plate on the appropriate insert on the microscope stage.
Locate the focal plane where the tracer beads are and ensure they appear evenly dispersed in the field of view.
Mark the specific position where cells form a confluent monolayer.
Mix two positions per well for a total of 48 positions.
Ensure the microscope’s autofocus system is on to prevent drift in the z-direction.
Correct any drift occurring in the x-y direction manually if necessary.
Set the time interval for acquisition settings to 10 min (images acquired every 10 min).
Select multi-channel acquisition mode.
Use a DAPI filter cube to image cell nuclei.
Use a GFP filter cube to image GFP-expressing bacteria.
Use an mCherry filter cube to image tracer beads.
Initiate the time-lapse image acquisition.
Expose ECs to Bb-GFP during microscopy recording.
Spin down the desired volume of live or heat-inactivated Bb-GFP for 5 min at 2,000 × g.
Wash the pellet once with PBS to remove the BSK culture media.
Spin down the bacteria for 5 min at 2,000 × g.
Resuspend bacteria in PBS so that 10 μL of bacterial suspension is added to each well of a 24-well plate.
Carefully remove the lid of the multi-well plate for image acquisition stoppage and remaining 10 minutes before the next time point.
Add 10 μL of bacterial suspension in PBS at the center of each well without disturbing the plate.
Add 10 μL of PBS alone to control wells (no bacteria, vehicle control).
Place the lid back on the multi-well plate after adding solutions.
Allow time-lapse imaging to continue for approximately 24 hours.
Carefully remove the lid from the multi-well plate once microscopy recording ends.
Add 500 μL of 10% SDS in water to each well.
Ensure cells have detached from the surface of the hydrogel through phase contrast imaging.
Take a fluorescence image of the tracer beads using the same power and exposure time as during time-lapse imaging.
Use images of EC nuclei to characterize changes in EC kinematics before and after exposure to Bb.
Analyze HMEC-1 cell motility pre- and post-exposure to Bb-GFP using representative overlays of phase contrast images and Hoechst-stained nuclei.
Place time-lapse images of HMEC-1 nuclei into a folder as individual 16-bit tiff files.
Perform PIV by comparing subsequent frames using the urapiv.m function.
Run the run_PIV.m script to calculate displacement vectors and store them as .txt files.
Inspect vector displacements (ux and uy) by running the Correlation_WT.m script.
Run the Correlation_WT.m script.
Calculate the average magnitude of displacements as a function of time while running the script.
Divide by the time interval between frames to calculate mean speed of cells.
Save output EC kinematical analysis as a .mat file.
Input various parameters (e.g., speed over time, correlation length) into Prism for statistical analysis.
Measure ECM displacements to perform TFM and monolayer stress microscopy.
Place time-lapse images of fluorescent tracer beads in a folder as individual 16-bit tiff files.
Add reference image tiff file with the name corresponding to the last frame acquired after SDS addition (e.g., beads101.tiff if 100 frames were taken).
Perform PIV using urapiv.m file by comparing each frame with the reference frame.
Use appropriate window size and overlap based on objective used and tracer bead size.
